sentences.en: If I have the money, I will buy an electric car.
sentences.de: Wenn ich das Geld habe, werde ich ein Elektroauto kaufen.

sentences.en: If the president were here, he would tell us what to do.
sentences.de: Wenn der Präsident hier wäre, würde er uns sagen, was zu tun ist.

sentences.en: If the gunman had come through the garden, he would have left some footprints.
sentences.de: Wäre der Täter durch den Garten gekommen, hätte er Fußspuren hinterlassen.

birkenbihl.title: Modal Verbs – Beispielsätze aus dem Buch

sentences.en: In parks, dogs must be kept on a lead.
sentences.de: In Parks müssen Hunde an der Leine geführt werden.

sentences.en: When Joe was younger, he could swim pretty fast.
sentences.de: Als Joe jünger war, konnte er ziemlich schnell schwimmen.

sentences.en: Pat has been able to play the piano for five years.
sentences.de: Pat kann seit fünf Jahren Klavier spielen.

birkenbihl.title: Reported Speech – Beispielsätze aus dem Buch

sentences.en: Tom said to me that he would wait for me at the train station.
sentences.de: (Direkt: "I will wait for you at the train station.") Tom sagte mir, dass er am Bahnhof auf mich warten würde.

sentences.en: Pat asked me what I was going to do the next day.
sentences.de: (Direkt: "What are you going to do tomorrow?") Pat fragte mich, was ich am nächsten Tag vorhätte.

sentences.en: Our teacher said that the earth moves around the sun.
sentences.de: Allgemeingültige Aussagen behalten die Present Tense – kein Backshift.

birkenbihl.title: Mixed Tenses – Beispielsätze aus dem Buch

sentences.en: Look! A spider is climbing up the wall.
sentences.de: Schau! Eine Spinne klettert gerade die Wand hinauf. (Signalwort Look! → Present Progressive)

sentences.en: Since 1990 we have been living in the country.
sentences.de: Seit 1990 leben wir auf dem Land. (since → Present Perfect (Progressive))

sentences.en: When I came home yesterday, he was sitting asleep in his armchair.
sentences.de: Als ich gestern heimkam, saß er schlafend in seinem Lehnstuhl. (Hintergrundhandlung → Past Progressive)

exercises.title: Challenge 1 – Mixed Types
exercises.instruction: Setze die richtige Verbform ein (Conditional Typ 0–III, auch gemischt).

parts: 1. If I have the money, I
questions.solutionEn: If I have the money, I will buy an electric car.
questions.solutionDe: Wenn ich das Geld habe, kaufe ich ein Elektroauto.
questions.explain: Typ I (real): if + Present → will + Infinitiv.

parts: (try) to stop eating so much junk food.
questions.solutionEn: If I were you, I would try to stop eating so much junk food.
questions.solutionDe: An deiner Stelle würde ich versuchen, weniger Junkfood zu essen.
questions.explain: Typ II: if + Past (were) → would + Infinitiv.

parts: (can) talk to Jorge if you had learnt some Spanish.
questions.solutionEn: You could talk to Jorge if you had learnt some Spanish.
questions.solutionDe: Du könntest (jetzt) mit Jorge reden, wenn du Spanisch gelernt hättest.
questions.explain: Mixed Conditional: Bedingung Vergangenheit (had learnt), Folge Gegenwart → could + Infinitiv.

parts: (burn) if you expose it to air.
questions.solutionEn: Phosphorus burns if you expose it to air.
questions.solutionDe: Phosphor brennt, wenn man ihn der Luft aussetzt.
questions.explain: Typ 0 (Naturgesetz): Present + Present.

parts: (stop) snowing, we will go skiing in the afternoon.
questions.solutionEn: If it stops snowing, we will go skiing in the afternoon.
questions.solutionDe: Wenn es aufhört zu schneien, gehen wir am Nachmittag Skifahren.
questions.explain: Typ I: kein will im if-Satz!

parts: (come) through the garden, he would have left some footprints.
questions.solutionEn: If the gunman had come through the garden, he would have left some footprints.
questions.solutionDe: Wäre der Täter durch den Garten gekommen, hätte er Fußspuren hinterlassen.
questions.explain: Typ III: if + Past Perfect → would have + Past Participle.

parts: 7. If the president were here, he
questions.solutionEn: If the president were here, he would tell us what to do.
questions.solutionDe: Wäre der Präsident hier, würde er uns sagen, was zu tun ist.
questions.explain: Typ II: were → would + Infinitiv.

parts: 8. She probably would not have developed an eating disorder if her parents
(support) her more when she was a teenager.
questions.solutionEn: She probably would not have developed an eating disorder if her parents had supported her more when she was a teenager.
questions.solutionDe: Sie hätte vermutlich keine Essstörung entwickelt, wenn ihre Eltern sie als Teenager mehr unterstützt hätten.
questions.explain: Typ III: would have + Partizip ↔ if + Past Perfect.

parts: 9. If you had not bought this big old house, you
(not must pay) such high costs every month.
questions.solutionEn: If you had not bought this big old house, you would not have to pay such high costs every month.
questions.solutionDe: Hättest du dieses große alte Haus nicht gekauft, müsstest du jetzt nicht jeden Monat so hohe Kosten zahlen.
questions.explain: Mixed: Bedingung Vergangenheit, Folge Gegenwart (every month) → would not have to pay.

parts: (need) another planet if we go on wasting resources like that.
questions.solutionEn: We will need another planet if we go on wasting resources like that.
questions.solutionDe: Wir werden einen zweiten Planeten brauchen, wenn wir so weiter Ressourcen verschwenden.
questions.explain: Typ I: if + Present (go on) → will + Infinitiv.

parts: 11. If the government had not passed laws to cut down emissions, more than half of our woods
(die) due to acid rain in the 1970s.
questions.solutionEn: If the government had not passed laws to cut down emissions, more than half of our woods would have died due to acid rain in the 1970s.
questions.solutionDe: Hätte die Regierung keine Emissions-Gesetze beschlossen, wäre in den 1970ern mehr als die Hälfte unserer Wälder durch sauren Regen gestorben.
questions.explain: Typ III (Vergangenheit, 1970s): would have + Past Participle.

parts: 12. If the film 'The Sound of Music' were not watched all over the world, a lot fewer tourists
questions.solutionEn: If the film 'The Sound of Music' were not watched all over the world, a lot fewer tourists would come to Austria every year.
questions.solutionDe: Würde 'The Sound of Music' nicht weltweit gesehen, kämen jedes Jahr viel weniger Touristen nach Österreich.
questions.explain: Typ II (unreale Gegenwart, every year): would + Infinitiv.

exercises.title: Challenge 2 – Mixed Types: Situations
exercises.instruction: Vervollständige den Satz sinnvoll – achte auf den richtigen Conditional-Typ. (Beispielantworten; wichtig ist die Zeitform.)

parts: 1. Do not do that. You will get into trouble if
questions.solutionEn: You will get into trouble if you do it again.
questions.solutionDe: Du bekommst Ärger, wenn du das noch einmal machst.
questions.explain: Typ I: will im Hauptsatz → Present im if-Satz.

parts: 2. We cannot leave Grandpa alone anymore. If he had not dropped in at his flat this morning,

opts: nobody would have noticed that Grandpa needed help
nobody will notice that Grandpa needs help
nobody noticed that Grandpa needed help

questions.solutionEn: If he had not dropped in at his flat this morning, nobody would have noticed that Grandpa needed help.
questions.solutionDe: Wäre er heute Früh nicht vorbeigeschaut, hätte niemand bemerkt, dass Opa Hilfe brauchte.
questions.explain: Typ III: if + Past Perfect → would have + Partizip.

parts: 3. To be honest, your suit would look a lot better if
questions.solutionEn: Your suit would look a lot better if you ironed it.
questions.solutionDe: Dein Anzug sähe viel besser aus, wenn du ihn bügeln würdest.
questions.explain: Typ II: would im Hauptsatz → Past im if-Satz.

parts: 4. I think he is only after her money. He would not have proposed to her if

opts: she had not been so rich
she would not be so rich

questions.solutionEn: He would not have proposed to her if she had not been so rich.
questions.solutionDe: Er hätte ihr keinen Antrag gemacht, wenn sie nicht so reich gewesen wäre.
questions.explain: Typ III: would have → if + Past Perfect.

parts: 5. He is not fit enough for the Olympics. If he trained harder,

opts: he would have a chance to qualify
he will have a chance to qualify
he would have had a chance to qualify

questions.solutionEn: If he trained harder, he would have a chance to qualify.
questions.solutionDe: Wenn er härter trainierte, hätte er eine Chance, sich zu qualifizieren.
questions.explain: Typ II: if + Past (trained) → would + Infinitiv.

parts: 6. I had to do a lot of overtime this week. I would have learnt more if

opts: I had had more time to study
I have more time to study
I would have more time to study

questions.solutionEn: I would have learnt more if I had had more time to study.
questions.solutionDe: Ich hätte mehr gelernt, wenn ich mehr Zeit zum Lernen gehabt hätte.
questions.explain: Typ III: would have learnt → if + Past Perfect (had had).

parts: 7. You must look after your garden better. The flowers will die if

opts: you do not water them regularly
you did not water them regularly

questions.solutionEn: The flowers will die if you do not water them regularly.
questions.solutionDe: Die Blumen gehen ein, wenn du sie nicht regelmäßig gießt.
questions.explain: Typ I: will im Hauptsatz → Present im if-Satz (kein will!).

parts: 8. We had to stay at home all weekend. If it had not been raining,
questions.solutionEn: If it had not been raining, we would have gone hiking.
questions.solutionDe: Hätte es nicht geregnet, wären wir wandern gegangen.
questions.explain: Typ III: if + Past Perfect → would have + Partizip.

parts: 9. Tom refuses to share housework. If his wife had a full-time job,

opts: he would have to help in the household
he will have to help in the household
he had to help in the household

questions.solutionEn: If his wife had a full-time job, he would have to help in the household.
questions.solutionDe: Hätte seine Frau einen Vollzeitjob, müsste er im Haushalt helfen.
questions.explain: Typ II: if + Past (had) → would + Infinitiv.

parts: 10. Global warming is a serious problem. If the polar ice caps melt,
questions.solutionEn: If the polar ice caps melt, sea levels will rise.
questions.solutionDe: Wenn die Polkappen schmelzen, steigt der Meeresspiegel.
questions.explain: Typ I (reale Gefahr): if + Present → will + Infinitiv.

exercises.title: Challenge 1 – Modale Ersatzformen
exercises.instruction: Setze die passende Form des Modalverbs ein (deutsche Vorgabe in Klammern). Achtung: Vergangenheit und Zukunft brauchen Ersatzformen!

parts: 1. Mr Brown broke his leg last week. So he
(nicht können) go out for seven days.
questions.solutionEn: So he could not go out for seven days.
questions.solutionDe: Er konnte sieben Tage lang nicht hinausgehen.
questions.explain: nicht können in der Vergangenheit → could not / was not able to.

questions.solutionEn: In parks dogs must be kept on a lead.
questions.solutionDe: In Parks müssen Hunde an der Leine geführt werden.
questions.explain: müssen (Vorschrift) → must / have to.

questions.solutionEn: Even experts can make mistakes.
questions.solutionDe: Sogar Experten können Fehler machen.
questions.explain: können (Möglichkeit) → can.

questions.solutionEn: When Joe was younger, he could swim pretty fast.
questions.solutionDe: Als Joe jünger war, konnte er ziemlich schnell schwimmen.
questions.explain: können in der Vergangenheit → could.

parts: (dürfen) I go to the disco tonight?" – Father: "No, you
questions.solutionEn: "May I go to the disco tonight?" – "No, you may not."
questions.solutionDe: „Darf ich heute Abend in die Disco?“ – „Nein, du darfst nicht.“
questions.explain: dürfen → may (höfliche Erlaubnisfrage).

parts: (dürfen) go when you are as old as Sue."
questions.solutionEn: "But Sue was allowed to go last week!" – "You will be allowed to go when you are as old as Sue."
questions.solutionDe: „Aber Sue durfte letzte Woche!“ – „Du wirst gehen dürfen, wenn du so alt bist wie Sue.“
questions.explain: dürfen hat keine Vergangenheits-/Zukunftsform → Ersatzform be allowed to (last week → was; Zukunft → will be).

parts: (nicht können) help us tomorrow. He is ill. That is why we
questions.solutionEn: Mr Brown will not be able to help us tomorrow. That is why we will have to work alone.
questions.solutionDe: Mr Brown wird uns morgen nicht helfen können, deshalb werden wir allein arbeiten müssen.
questions.explain: Zukunft (tomorrow): können → will be able to; müssen → will have to.

parts: (nicht brauchen) phone her, because she is not at home at the moment.
questions.solutionEn: You need not phone her, because she is not at home at the moment.
questions.solutionDe: Du brauchst sie nicht anzurufen, sie ist gerade nicht zu Hause.
questions.explain: nicht brauchen → need not / do not need to. must not wäre ein Verbot!

questions.solutionEn: You must do as I say.
questions.solutionDe: Du musst tun, was ich sage.
questions.explain: müssen (Befehl des Sprechers) → must.

parts: (nicht müssen) be at home before midnight.
questions.solutionEn: Pat does not have to be at home before midnight.
questions.solutionDe: Pat muss nicht vor Mitternacht zu Hause sein.
questions.explain: nicht müssen → does not have to / need not (≠ must not = Verbot!).

parts: (eigentlich nicht sollen) eat many sweets. Instead, they
questions.solutionEn: Children should not eat many sweets. Instead, they should eat more fruit.
questions.solutionDe: Kinder sollten eigentlich nicht viele Süßigkeiten essen, sondern mehr Obst.
questions.explain: (nicht) sollen als Rat → should (not) / ought (not) to.

parts: (können) play the piano for five years.
questions.solutionEn: Pat can play the piano. He has been able to play the piano for five years.
questions.solutionDe: Pat kann Klavier spielen – schon seit fünf Jahren.
questions.explain: for five years → Present Perfect: Ersatzform has been able to (can hat kein Perfekt).

questions.solutionEn: There must be a mistake.
questions.solutionDe: Da muss ein Fehler vorliegen.
questions.explain: must = logische Schlussfolgerung („das muss so sein“).

parts: (müssen) work very hard for their A-levels next year.
questions.solutionEn: The students will have to work very hard for their A-levels next year.
questions.solutionDe: Die Schüler werden nächstes Jahr für die Matura hart arbeiten müssen.
questions.explain: next year → Zukunft: müssen → will have to.

parts: (können) wake up the baby, and then mother will be angry.
questions.solutionEn: We must be quiet. Otherwise, we could wake up the baby.
questions.solutionDe: Wir müssen leise sein, sonst könnten wir das Baby aufwecken.
questions.explain: könnten (Möglichkeit) → could/might.

parts: 15. Mr Smith missed the train. He
(nicht können) go to Vienna at seven and
(müssen) wait for the nine o'clock train instead.
questions.solutionEn: He could not go to Vienna at seven and had to wait for the nine o'clock train instead.
questions.solutionDe: Er konnte nicht um sieben nach Wien fahren und musste stattdessen auf den Neun-Uhr-Zug warten.
questions.explain: Vergangenheit: können → could, müssen → had to.

parts: 16. Alice got top marks in her A-levels. So she
questions.solutionEn: So she must be very clever.
questions.solutionDe: Sie muss also sehr klug sein.
questions.explain: must = logische Schlussfolgerung aus den Topnoten.

parts: (können) swim the English Channel soon. They
(nicht brauchen) clean everything before they started to paint.
questions.solutionEn: She will be able to swim the English Channel soon. They did not need to clean everything before they started to paint.
questions.solutionDe: Sie wird bald den Ärmelkanal durchschwimmen können. / Sie brauchten nicht alles zu putzen, bevor sie zu malen begannen.
questions.explain: soon → will be able to; nicht brauchen (Vergangenheit) → did not need to / did not have to.

exercises.title: Zeit- und Ortsangaben verschieben
exercises.instruction: Wie verschieben sich die Angaben in der indirekten Rede?

questions.solutionEn: now → then, today → that day, here → there, this → that
questions.solutionDe: jetzt → damals, heute → an jenem Tag, hier → dort, dieses → jenes
questions.explain: In der indirekten Rede rücken Zeit- und Ortsangaben eine Stufe „weiter weg“.

questions.solutionEn: these → those, ago → before, yesterday → the day before, last week → the week before
questions.solutionDe: diese → jene, vor → davor, gestern → am Tag davor, letzte Woche → die Woche davor
questions.explain: ago wird zu before; yesterday/last week wandern eine Stufe zurück.

questions.solutionEn: tomorrow → the next day / the following day, the day after tomorrow → in two days' time, the day before yesterday → two days before, next week → the following week
questions.solutionDe: morgen → am nächsten Tag, übermorgen → in zwei Tagen, vorgestern → zwei Tage davor, nächste Woche → die folgende Woche
questions.explain: Zukunftsangaben → following/next-Formen.

exercises.title: Your Turn 1 – Reported Speech
exercises.instruction: Setze die direkte Rede in die indirekte Rede (Backshift, Pronomen, Zeitangaben!).

parts: 1. Tom said to me, "I will wait for you at the train station." → Tom said to me that
questions.solutionEn: Tom said to me that he would wait for me at the train station.
questions.solutionDe: Tom sagte mir, dass er am Bahnhof auf mich warten würde.
questions.explain: will → would; I/you → he/me.

parts: 2. Pat asked me, "What are you going to do tomorrow?" → Pat asked me what
questions.solutionEn: Pat asked me what I was going to do the next day.
questions.solutionDe: Pat fragte mich, was ich am nächsten Tag vorhätte.
questions.explain: Frage: kein do-Umstellung, are → was, tomorrow → the next day.

parts: 3. Jason says, "I want to be a famous actor when I have grown up." → Jason says that he
to be a famous actor when he
questions.solutionEn: Jason says that he wants to be a famous actor when he has grown up.
questions.solutionDe: Jason sagt, dass er ein berühmter Schauspieler werden will, wenn er groß ist.
questions.explain: says = Present → KEIN Backshift, nur Pronomen ändern.

parts: 4. Mr Smith told his secretary, "You can phone from this office." → Mr Smith told his secretary that she
questions.solutionEn: Mr Smith told his secretary that she could phone from that office.
questions.solutionDe: Mr Smith sagte seiner Sekretärin, dass sie von jenem Büro aus telefonieren könne.
questions.explain: can → could; this → that.

parts: 5. Pat said, "I am living with my parents at present, but I hope that I will have my own flat soon." → Pat said that he
with his parents at that time, but he hoped that he
questions.solutionEn: Pat said that he was living with his parents at that time, but he hoped that he would have his own flat soon.
questions.solutionDe: Pat sagte, er wohne derzeit bei den Eltern, hoffe aber, bald eine eigene Wohnung zu haben.
questions.explain: am living → was living; will → would; at present → at that time.

parts: 6. Jill said, "I usually take my dog for a walk after work." → Jill said that she usually
her dog for a walk after work.
questions.solutionEn: Jill said that she usually took her dog for a walk after work.
questions.solutionDe: Jill sagte, dass sie ihren Hund nach der Arbeit normalerweise spazieren führe.
questions.explain: Backshift Present → Past. Bei Gewohnheiten wäre auch „takes“ erlaubt (Regel b im Buch).

parts: 7. He asked me, "Have you ever met her before?" → He asked me
questions.solutionEn: He asked me if I had ever met her before.
questions.solutionDe: Er fragte mich, ob ich sie je zuvor getroffen hätte.
questions.explain: Ja/Nein-Frage → if/whether; Present Perfect → Past Perfect.

parts: 8. Mary said, "The party last Saturday was great. We were dancing all night long." → Mary said that the party
questions.solutionEn: Mary said that the party the Saturday before had been great and that they had been dancing all night long.
questions.solutionDe: Mary sagte, die Party am Samstag davor sei großartig gewesen und sie hätten die ganze Nacht getanzt.
questions.explain: last Saturday → the Saturday before; was → had been; were dancing → had been dancing.

parts: 9. Lucy said, "In this village nothing ever happens." → Lucy said that in
questions.solutionEn: Lucy said that in that village nothing ever happened.
questions.solutionDe: Lucy sagte, dass in jenem Dorf nie etwas passiere.
questions.explain: this → that; happens → happened (bei Allgemeingültigem auch „happens“ möglich).

parts: 10. Tim said, "I have missed my train. So I will be late for work today." → Tim said that he
questions.solutionEn: Tim said that he had missed his train, so he would be late for work that day.
questions.solutionDe: Tim sagte, er habe seinen Zug verpasst und werde an jenem Tag zu spät zur Arbeit kommen.
questions.explain: Present Perfect → Past Perfect; will → would; today → that day.

parts: 11. The shop assistant said, "The sales already started last weekend." → The shop assistant said that the sales
questions.solutionEn: The shop assistant said that the sales had already started the weekend before.
questions.solutionDe: Die Verkäuferin sagte, der Schlussverkauf habe schon am Wochenende davor begonnen.
questions.explain: Past → Past Perfect; last weekend → the weekend before.

parts: 12. Father says to John, "Tomorrow we are going to meet Granny." → Father says to John that

opts: tomorrow they are going to meet
the next day they were going to meet
tomorrow we were going to meet

questions.solutionEn: Father says to John that tomorrow they are going to meet Granny.
questions.solutionDe: Vater sagt zu John, dass sie morgen Oma treffen werden.
questions.explain: says = Present → kein Backshift, tomorrow bleibt tomorrow!

parts: 13. Sue asked Ann, "Did you like your last holiday?" → Sue asked Ann
questions.solutionEn: Sue asked Ann if she had liked her last holiday.
questions.solutionDe: Sue fragte Ann, ob ihr der letzte Urlaub gefallen habe.
questions.explain: Frage mit did → if + Past Perfect; keine Frage-Wortstellung.

parts: 14. Mr Johnson asked, "May I use your phone, sir?" → Mr Johnson asked
questions.solutionEn: Mr Johnson asked if he might use his phone.
questions.solutionDe: Mr Johnson fragte, ob er sein Telefon benutzen dürfe.
questions.explain: may → might; Anrede „sir“ fällt weg.

parts: 15. Father told mum, "You do not have to water the flowers. I have already done it for you." → Father told mum that she
questions.solutionEn: Father told mum that she did not have to water the flowers because he had already done it for her.
questions.solutionDe: Vater sagte Mama, sie müsse die Blumen nicht gießen, er habe es schon erledigt.
questions.explain: do not have to → did not have to; Present Perfect → Past Perfect.

parts: 16. Paul said, "I have just bought a new car." → Paul said that he
questions.solutionEn: Paul said that he had just bought a new car.
questions.solutionDe: Paul sagte, er habe sich gerade ein neues Auto gekauft.
questions.explain: Present Perfect → Past Perfect; just bleibt.

exercises.title: Super Challenge 1 – Mixed Tenses (Teil 1: 1–13)
exercises.instruction: Setze die richtige Zeitform ein. Achte auf Signalwörter!

questions.solutionEn: Look! A spider is climbing up the wall.
questions.solutionDe: Schau! Eine Spinne klettert gerade die Wand hinauf.
questions.explain: Look! → Present Progressive (passiert gerade).

questions.solutionEn: Yesterday, while father was doing the washing up, mother was working in the garden.
questions.solutionDe: Gestern, während Vater abwusch, arbeitete Mutter im Garten.
questions.explain: while + zwei parallele Handlungen → Past Progressive.

parts: (stay) in a luxury hotel in Manhattan for ten days."
questions.solutionEn: "Have you ever been to New York?" – "Yes, I was there last August. We stayed in a luxury hotel in Manhattan for ten days."
questions.solutionDe: „Warst du je in New York?“ – „Ja, letzten August. Wir wohnten zehn Tage in einem Luxushotel.“
questions.explain: ever → Present Perfect; last August (abgeschlossene Zeit) → Past Simple.

parts: (get) up at six in the morning, but today he
(not get up) that early because it
questions.solutionEn: John usually gets up at six in the morning, but today he is not getting up that early because it is Sunday.
questions.solutionDe: John steht normalerweise um sechs auf, aber heute nicht so früh, weil Sonntag ist.
questions.explain: usually → Present Simple; today (Ausnahme) → Present Progressive.

questions.solutionEn: I hope the weather will be fine tomorrow.
questions.solutionDe: Ich hoffe, das Wetter wird morgen schön.
questions.explain: tomorrow + Vorhersage → will-Future.

questions.solutionEn: Sue was doing the ironing, when someone rang at the door.
questions.solutionDe: Sue bügelte gerade, als jemand an der Tür läutete.
questions.explain: Hintergrundhandlung → Past Progressive; Unterbrechung → Past Simple.

questions.solutionEn: She stood up, went downstairs and opened the door.
questions.solutionDe: Sie stand auf, ging hinunter und öffnete die Tür.
questions.explain: Handlungskette in der Vergangenheit → Past Simple.

parts: (have) an English exam tomorrow. So they
questions.solutionEn: The students have an English exam tomorrow. So they have been studying a lot since last week.
questions.solutionDe: Die Schüler haben morgen eine Englisch-Prüfung, darum lernen sie seit letzter Woche viel.
questions.explain: since → Present Perfect (Progressive); fixer Termin → Present Simple.

parts: (go) to the cinema with his friends.
questions.solutionEn: After Tom had finished work, he went to the cinema with his friends.
questions.solutionDe: Nachdem Tom die Arbeit beendet hatte, ging er mit Freunden ins Kino.
questions.explain: after + Vorvergangenheit → Past Perfect, danach Past Simple.

parts: 10. At the moment the members of the team
questions.solutionEn: At the moment the members of the team are listening to their boss.
questions.solutionDe: Im Moment hören die Teammitglieder ihrem Chef zu.
questions.explain: at the moment → Present Progressive.

parts: (move) to Australia in 2005. Since then they
questions.solutionEn: Ben and Jenny moved to Australia in 2005. Since then they have been living in Sydney.
questions.solutionDe: Ben und Jenny zogen 2005 nach Australien. Seitdem leben sie in Sydney.
questions.explain: in 2005 → Past Simple; since then → Present Perfect (Progressive).

questions.solutionEn: When they were watching TV, the telephone rang.
questions.solutionDe: Als sie fernsahen, läutete das Telefon.
questions.explain: Hintergrund → Past Progressive; kurzes Ereignis → Past Simple.

questions.solutionEn: Granny will be 80 next week. "What are you doing in your holidays?" – "Well, we do not know."
questions.solutionDe: Oma wird nächste Woche 80. „Was macht ihr in den Ferien?“ – „Wir wissen es nicht.“
questions.explain: next week → will; geplante Zukunft → Present Progressive; know = Zustandsverb → nie Progressive.

exercises.title: Super Challenge 1 – Mixed Tenses (Teil 2: 13–22)
exercises.instruction: Setze die richtige Zeitform ein. Achte auf Signalwörter!

parts: (not want) to go to Italy again as we
questions.solutionEn: I do not want to go to Italy again as we were there last year.
questions.solutionDe: Ich will nicht wieder nach Italien, wir waren letztes Jahr dort.
questions.explain: Gegenwart → Present Simple; last year → Past Simple.

parts: (want) to go to Sweden or Norway, but the children
(love) swimming in the sea and playing on the beach. They really
questions.solutionEn: I want to go to Sweden or Norway, but the children loved swimming in the sea and playing on the beach. They really enjoyed it last year.
questions.solutionDe: Ich will nach Schweden oder Norwegen, aber die Kinder liebten das Schwimmen im Meer – sie haben es letztes Jahr richtig genossen.
questions.explain: last year → Past Simple (loved, enjoyed).

parts: (not make) up our minds, but I hope that we
questions.solutionEn: Therefore we have not made up our minds, but I hope that we will agree on a destination next weekend.
questions.solutionDe: Darum haben wir uns noch nicht entschieden, aber ich hoffe, wir einigen uns nächstes Wochenende.
questions.explain: Ergebnis bis jetzt → Present Perfect; next weekend → will-Future.

questions.solutionEn: I promise that I will not tell anybody about the accident.
questions.solutionDe: Ich verspreche, ich erzähle niemandem von dem Unfall.
questions.explain: Versprechen → will-Future.

questions.solutionEn: "What time does the train leave?" – "It usually leaves at 6.30, but today it is leaving ten minutes later."
questions.solutionDe: „Wann fährt der Zug?“ – „Normalerweise um 6.30, aber heute zehn Minuten später.“
questions.explain: Fahrplan → Present Simple; heutige Ausnahme → Present Progressive.

questions.solutionEn: When we were playing tennis last Sunday it suddenly started to rain.
questions.solutionDe: Als wir letzten Sonntag Tennis spielten, begann es plötzlich zu regnen.
questions.explain: Hintergrund → Past Progressive; suddenly → Past Simple.

questions.solutionEn: The dancing club has its summer party in July.
questions.solutionDe: Der Tanzklub hat sein Sommerfest im Juli.
questions.explain: Regelmäßiges Ereignis → Present Simple.

questions.solutionEn: Our friends had organised everything before they left.
questions.solutionDe: Unsere Freunde hatten alles organisiert, bevor sie abreisten.
questions.explain: before: Vorvergangenheit → Past Perfect, dann Past Simple.

parts: (be) renovated last March to the couple.
questions.solutionEn: The travel agent recommended the hotel which was renovated last March to the couple.
questions.solutionDe: Der Reiseberater empfahl dem Paar das Hotel, das letzten März renoviert wurde.
questions.explain: last March → Past Simple (Passiv: was renovated).

questions.solutionEn: Sue had already finished her work when Jim called.
questions.solutionDe: Sue hatte ihre Arbeit schon beendet, als Jim anrief.
questions.explain: already + Vorvergangenheit → Past Perfect.

parts: (you, spend) your next summer holidays?" – "My family and I
questions.solutionEn: "Where are you spending your next summer holidays?" – "My family and I are flying to Spain."
questions.solutionDe: „Wo verbringt ihr die nächsten Sommerferien?“ – „Wir fliegen nach Spanien.“
questions.explain: Geplante Zukunft → Present Progressive.

questions.solutionEn: Granny did not tell us that she had been ill last week.
questions.solutionDe: Oma erzählte uns nicht, dass sie letzte Woche krank gewesen war.
questions.explain: Erzählzeit Past → davor Past Perfect.

exercises.title: Super Challenge 1 – Mixed Tenses (Teil 3: 23–33)
exercises.instruction: Setze die richtige Zeitform ein. Achte auf Signalwörter!

questions.solutionEn: Mother expects that her children will be at home for lunch.
questions.solutionDe: Mutter erwartet, dass die Kinder zum Mittagessen zu Hause sein werden.
questions.explain: Erwartung an die Zukunft → will-Future.

questions.solutionEn: Many people believe that humankind will never fly to Mars.
questions.solutionDe: Viele glauben, dass die Menschheit nie zum Mars fliegen wird.
questions.explain: Zukunftsglaube → will-Future.

parts: (you, go) to the cinema last week?" – "No, I
questions.solutionEn: "Did you go to the cinema last week?" – "No, I did not go because I was there three weeks ago."
questions.solutionDe: „Warst du letzte Woche im Kino?“ – „Nein, ich war schon vor drei Wochen dort.“
questions.explain: last week / ago → Past Simple.

parts: (live) in the country, but next year we
questions.solutionEn: Since 1990 we have been living in the country, but next year we will move to a big city.
questions.solutionDe: Seit 1990 leben wir auf dem Land, aber nächstes Jahr ziehen wir in eine Großstadt.
questions.explain: since → Present Perfect (Progressive); next year → will-Future.

questions.solutionEn: Many years ago John studied Spanish and French abroad.
questions.solutionDe: Vor vielen Jahren studierte John im Ausland Spanisch und Französisch.
questions.explain: ago → Past Simple.

questions.solutionEn: The secretary has just finished writing the letters.
questions.solutionDe: Die Sekretärin hat die Briefe gerade fertig geschrieben.
questions.explain: just (gerade eben) → Present Perfect.

questions.solutionEn: When I came home yesterday, he was sitting asleep in his armchair.
questions.solutionDe: Als ich gestern heimkam, saß er schlafend im Lehnstuhl.
questions.explain: Ereignis → Past Simple; Hintergrundzustand → Past Progressive.

questions.solutionEn: After the children had gone home for lunch, they had an appointment with the dentist.
questions.solutionDe: Nachdem die Kinder zum Mittagessen heimgegangen waren, hatten sie einen Zahnarzttermin.
questions.explain: after → Past Perfect, Hauptsatz Past Simple.

questions.solutionEn: "Since when have you had your new bike?" – "I bought it last Saturday."
questions.solutionDe: „Seit wann hast du dein neues Rad?“ – „Ich habe es letzten Samstag gekauft.“
questions.explain: since when → Present Perfect; last Saturday → Past Simple.

questions.solutionEn: Jason told the police that there had been an accident in Park Avenue.
questions.solutionDe: Jason erzählte der Polizei, dass es in der Park Avenue einen Unfall gegeben hatte.
questions.explain: Indirekte Rede nach told → Past Perfect.

parts: 33. Since his wife left home, Patrick
questions.solutionEn: Since his wife left home, Patrick has been preparing breakfast on his own.
questions.solutionDe: Seit seine Frau ausgezogen ist, macht Patrick das Frühstück allein.
questions.explain: since → Present Perfect Progressive (andauernd bis jetzt).
